mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the second law of thermodynamics is a common misconception?

options.A: Heat can spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without any external work.
options.B: In an isolated system, the total entropy never decreases.
options.C: No heat engine can be 100% efficient.
options.D: The direction of natural processes is determined by an increase in entropy.

mcqs.answer: Heat can spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without any external work.
mcqs.explanation: The second law states that heat spontaneously flows from a hotter to a colder body; the opposite direction requires external work. Options B, C, and D correctly reflect the qualitative statements of the second law, while option A is a misconception.

mcqs.question: Two bodies, one at 350 K and the other at 300 K, are placed in thermal contact. Which direction will the heat flow spontaneously?

options.A: From the 300 K body to the 350 K body
options.B: From the 350 K body to the 300 K body
options.C: No net heat flow will occur
options.D: Heat will flow in both directions equally

mcqs.answer: From the 350 K body to the 300 K body
mcqs.explanation: According to the second law, heat flows spontaneously from a higher temperature (hotter) body to a lower temperature (colder) body. Hence heat moves from 350 K to 300 K. Option A reverses the direction, while C and D ignore the temperature gradient.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the limitation imposed by the second law on any heat engine?

options.A: No heat engine can convert all the heat it receives into work; its efficiency must be less than 100%.
options.B: All heat engines can achieve the same efficiency regardless of the temperatures of the reservoirs.
options.C: The efficiency of a heat engine depends only on the type of working fluid used.
options.D: Real engines can have efficiencies higher than that of an ideal Carnot engine operating between the same reservoirs.

mcqs.answer: No heat engine can convert all the heat it receives into work; its efficiency must be less than 100%.
mcqs.explanation: The second law limits the maximum possible efficiency to that of a Carnot engine, which is always less than 100% unless the cold reservoir is at absolute zero (impossible). Options B, C, and D contradict this fundamental limitation.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: Which of the following processes is reversible under ideal conditions?

options.A: Free expansion of a gas into a vacuum
options.B: Frictionless, quasistatic compression of a gas by a piston moving infinitesimally slowly
options.C: Mixing of two different gases in a container
options.D: Heat flow from a hot reservoir to a cold reservoir

mcqs.answer: Frictionless, quasistatic compression of a gas by a piston moving infinitesimally slowly
mcqs.explanation: A reversible process must be quasistatic and free of dissipative effects like friction or unrestrained expansion. Option B satisfies these criteria. Options A, C, and D are inherently irreversible because they involve spontaneous gradients or mixing.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand qualitative statement of second law
mcqs.question: The qualitative statement of the second law of thermodynamics is:

options.A: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
options.B: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
options.C: Heat always flows spontaneously from a colder body to a hotter body.
options.D: Work can be completely converted into heat without any loss.

mcqs.answer: The entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
mcqs.explanation: Option B captures the qualitative essence of the second law: in an isolated system, natural processes increase or keep constant the total entropy. Option A describes the first law, while C is opposite to the true direction of spontaneous heat flow, and D is a consequence of the first law, not the second.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations best illustrates spontaneous heat flow as described by the second law?

options.A: An ice cube placed in a room at 25 °C melts without any external work.
options.B: Water in a sealed container is heated to 100 °C while the surrounding air remains at 20 °C.
options.C: A cold metal rod is placed in contact with a hot metal rod, and heat flows from the cold rod to the hot rod.
options.D: A perfectly insulated box containing a gas shows no temperature change over time.

mcqs.answer: An ice cube placed in a room at 25 °C melts without any external work.
mcqs.explanation: The ice (colder) absorbs heat from the warmer surroundings, a spontaneous flow from hot to cold. Option B describes heating by an external source, not spontaneous flow. Option C reverses the natural direction, and option D involves no heat flow.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the limitation on the efficiency of any heat engine?

options.A: A heat engine can convert all the heat it receives into work.
options.B: A heat engine must operate between at least two thermal reservoirs.
options.C: No heat engine can have an efficiency greater than that of a Carnot engine working between the same two reservoirs.
options.D: A heat engine can produce work without any heat input.

mcqs.answer: No heat engine can have an efficiency greater than that of a Carnot engine working between the same two reservoirs.
mcqs.explanation: The Carnot efficiency sets the upper bound for any engine operating between given temperatures. Options A and D violate the second law, while B, though true, does not address the efficiency limitation.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level
mcqs.question: A gas expands slowly and isothermally against a piston that is kept in equilibrium with the external pressure at every instant. Which description best fits this process?

options.D: Irreversible heat flow from cold to hot

mcqs.explanation: A quasistatic, frictionless, isothermal expansion where the external pressure matches the internal pressure at each step is reversible. Options B, C, and D describe inherently irreversible processes.
